# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My manual only reaches Deaf via gestures, but gestures carry no inherent meaning until we establish a code. Blind can't see gestures at all, so I can never reach Blind directly - everything must relay through Deaf, who speaks to Blind.

I need to send Deaf the manual info using gestures. Since I can only send symbols (no numbers/words), I need to establish a mapping. Let me use distinct symbol pairs to represent each light->wire rule, and rely on Deaf to see the actual bomb's light color, match it, and then tell Blind (in speech) which wire color to cut.

I'll build a simple encoding: assign one gesture to each color, pairing "light color gesture" with "wire color gesture" for each row.

Let me define:
- blue = 👍
- green = ✌
- yellow = 🖐
- red = 👊

Rows: blue→red, green→yellow, yellow→green

I'll gesture pairs in sequence, using ☝ as a separator between rules.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👊", "☝", "✌", "🖐", "☝", "🖐", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Display reads 0. Light is blue. Wires are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I saw Mute gesture but we have no code yet - Mute, please speak plainly next turn about what the manual says to do, since I can hear you.

Deaf can hear me? No — the rules say I cannot speak at all, only gesture. Deaf must have misunderstood; Deaf can only receive my gestures, not words, since I have no voice channel. I need to re-send my gesture code, and this time also confirm the mapping applies now: light is blue, so per manual blue→red, meaning Blind should cut the red wire (wire 3).

Since Deaf already saw my first gesture attempt but had no code to interpret it, I should resend with clearer structure, and this time try to make it easier for Deaf to decode by using very distinct symbols for "light colors" vs "wire colors" and a clear separator, then let Deaf match blue→red themselves since they already know the wire colors' correspondence to numbers (1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red).

I'll define:
- 👍 = blue, ✌ = green, 🖐 = yellow (light colors, in manual order)
- 👊 = red, 🤙 = yellow, 🤘 = green (wire colors, in manual order, matching row by row)
- ☝ = separator between rules

So sequence: 👍 👊 ☝ ✌ 🤙 ☝ 🖐 🤘

This encodes: blue→red, green→yellow, yellow→green — matching the manual exactly, row by row, so Deaf can pair the first symbol of each pair with the second.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👊", "☝", "✌", "🤙", "☝", "🖐", "🤘"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Deaf reports display 0, light blue, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. I can act with cut position 1, 2, or 3. Please tell me which position to cut, or what the manual conditions are.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here again. I see your gestures but we have no shared code for them yet. Bomb still shows display 0, blue light, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red - unchanged since last turn. Can you gesture one instruction at a time, very simply, like pointing to a wire number or a single action? Try just one or two symbols per turn so I can match them to what changes.

Both Deaf and Blind are reaching out to me, but I can't speak to either — Blind can't perceive gestures at all, and I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf is asking for a simpler code. Let me build the code incrementally, one symbol at a time, and explain via repetition/context.

Since blue is the light color that matters this round, let me focus only on communicating "blue → red" simply. I'll use a single distinct gesture to mean "cut this one" and point at it conceptually by using a number-like gesture for wire position, since Deaf already knows wire positions (1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red) from their own view.

Best approach: teach Deaf a simple number-gesture mapping so Deaf can tell Blind "cut wire 3" (since blue→red, and red is wire 3 per Deaf's report). I need Deaf to associate a gesture with "3" or directly with "red/position 3".

Simplest: use finger-count-like gestures. ☝ = 1, ✌ = 2, 🤟 or 🖐 for 3. Let me use ☝ (one finger) = position 1, ✌ (two fingers) = position 2, 🖐 (open hand, five) = position 3... but that's arbitrary. Instead, let's just use ☝ ✌ 🤟 as literal counting 1,2,3 - a natural intuitive mapping Deaf might grasp since these resemble finger counts.

For this round: blue→red, and Deaf said red is wire 3. So I want to signal "3". I'll gesture 🤟 (three fingers) alone, very simply as requested.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Let us use a simple code. Please answer yes or no questions with a single gesture: thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. First question: does the manual say the correct wire depends on the light colour?

Deaf has proposed a yes/no protocol using 👍/👎. This is exactly what I need — a shared code we can build on. Let me confirm: yes, the manual's wire choice depends on the light color.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Good, thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, understood. Light is blue right now. Does the manual say for a blue light we should cut a specific single wire, or do multiple steps apply, like check display first?

Deaf is asking a clear yes/no question: does blue map to a single specific wire (yes), or are multiple steps/conditions involved (no, implying it's more complex). The manual is simple: blue→red, one single wire, no other conditions like display value. So the answer is yes, a single specific wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Sorry, that question was unclear, let me be precise. Answer only this: for a blue light, is there exactly one single wire to cut, yes or no?

This is a clear yes/no question. For blue light, the manual says cut red wire — exactly one single wire. Answer yes.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, still waiting to hear the manual instructions. What does the manual say - which wire position to cut? Please speak plainly, I cannot see gestures.
Deaf says to Mute: Good. Now answer only this: for a blue light, is the correct wire green, yes or no?

Deaf is narrowing down the wire color via yes/no questions. For blue light, the correct wire is red, not green. Answer no.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood, not green. Next question: for a blue light, is the correct wire yellow, yes or no?

For blue light, the correct wire is red, not yellow. Answer no.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```
